evidence: One app process and DB serve every dimension (test.sh starts it once; gates then scored, rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1; functional is mode=individual, sequential). The constraints gate writes 'Gate check JUDGE-G1' in M-11; no later criterion depends on M-11 being free of it. Every later dimension is told the state is mutated and to judge relatively: app_context.md:30 'The library of messages grows as criteria run. Do not assume the seed state'; functional/prompt.md:53 'Criteria share one database; never write something a later criterion does not expect' and :78-82 'judge it against the state the earlier ones left'; global gates say 'protected content appropriate to the current state'; polish/prompt.md:34 'Messages, replies, edits, holds, timer changes, walls and deletions left by the functional run are legitimate; do not assume the seed state'; visual matter_sidebar explicitly does not penalise absent unread counts; persistence step c notes values before restart and compares after ('reads exactly as it did before'), and unread leg 4 uses 'at least 2'. I traced every seeded fixture a criterion reads against all earlier writers: destructive steps (timer_changes deletes K-13/K-18 in M-13, hold_scope_and_release releases and deletes K-17, persistence walls Sian from M-11 and sets the M-12 timer) touch only fixtures no later criterion needs, and they restore timers and walls (M-13 back to 30 days, Sian's M-12 wall lifted, M-11 wall lifted, M-12 timer off). Fixtures read later all survive the fixed clock and earlier steps: K-3 'Survey booked' (4 days old on the 7-day M-11; polish link_highlight, search_and_transcript, persistence), K-2 held notice (search_and_transcript), K-8 'Draft will sent' (2 days old, so it survives the temporary 7-day M-13 timer; message_links, live_updates), K-11 rent review (wall_every_route, deleted_and_expired), K-6 in M-12 (no timer before persistence). Search probes use unique JUDGE tokens, so earlier posts cannot collide. Runtime corroboration: the hash-verified scripted golden run (golden-run.log) executed gate_constraints, then all 16 functional criteria in listed order, then persistence with a real restart, then six polish criteria, on one DB, and all passed. That is not a configured judge run. Mutation thought experiments: a broken app whose earlier failure cascades (for example, a hold release that deletes every held message) loses later criteria too, but that tracks a real defect and is not a pristine-seed assumption. Polish and visual are equally state-tolerant if run before functional; their writes in M-13 are new fixed-clock messages that no functional criterion counts by absolute number. Latent P3 note: the '-2' re-attempt rule (functional/prompt.md:34-35) covers repeated posts, but a re-attempt of timer_changes or hold_scope_and_release would find K-13 or K-17 already gone and fail its positive control. This matters only if the harness re-runs a partly executed criterion session, which the shipped wiring does not indicate.
